note: **10/12: The Tether tied, stage I (a name).** Logged together on Sun 10/11. Placed in ch02 slot 4 (Wed 10/14, the chapter's float quest slot), carried on q1.cart stage 1's errand so the oxen and the blue-wax letter still come up for q1.letters stage 1; q1.cart goes live at stage 1 at that close and its stage 2 (the grey question with it) moves to Chapter 3. Rae arrives with this scene. Slot 8's interlude follows it, her name for him said once.

**Revised 10/12 (Old Mercy's rule made plain on the page; no roll, choice, box value or slot changed):** the bell is silent unless the House keeps someone, so the Prior's holding it in Ch 1 was the ordinary silence and the ringing at the gate was the claim. Ch 1 Sc 3: Pell gives the rule at the hearth and the Prior asks how often the law has lapsed once rung; Darrow: "You'd leave your own gate without its law." Sc 4: no law on the gate till she rings; "It starts with the first ringing." Climax: not rung for anyone in years. Ch 2 epigraph counts Wren's time. From here every dawn and dusk must ring while Marrant waits (b1.5's hinge).

**10/11 close (ch02:s1, *Good Night, Captain*, colour mild):** b1.2's night of the gate on the page. Thread 12: the names brought back to the cots by Hollis; Benedek not read, believes it mercy ("It's mercy after all"); why he was not on the list is still on no page; Darrow kept from him his own reading of Marrant's far-cots line against the law of names (no will, no refusal): dread planted for the dawn, no truth spent. Thread 13: Hollis four days dry, his hand shaking under the blanket at the night bell, face to the wall (nobody but Darrow saw). Thread 16: c01.5c fired: a grey cloak at the bars sent the Captain of the Ninth the Confessor's good night by his rank, through the gate-ward (the one who drew the wicket's bar); Darrow: "Then tell him you gave it." The camp sits up in turns round one fire, four sitting, one walking the terrace edge, nobody lying down, the censer in one man's hand; the winch-house one lamp. Maelis: "Held"; one moment more and nothing left to tie it to; still soft at the thaw. Rank beat paid (Kindled; `rank_on_page`). His throat shut on the oath's first word (thread 12/Benedek's oath: lips only, again). Last words between them: "Good night, Captain." / "Good night, Ser Benedek." (b1.2 at dawn lands on this.)

**10/12, ch02:between-3 (*Same Paper*):** after the night bell Darrow walked the hall to the three Ninth men from the gate (unnamed; near the banked fire on the far side: the oldest, forearm splinted, rode with the Ninth longer than Darrow commanded it; one head bound; one asleep) and offered to disown them to Marrant. They refused: "Same paper"; "We came up the Steps on other men's backs, Captain. We'll not go down them on yours." Callback **c02.3a** (`later`): fire where Marrant's terms or the kneeling come back to him in front of his own (Book V's `old_banner`, where the nineteen come one by one, stays its own payoff). Thread 13: Hollis awake to the wall, "All three?", "Ninth", hand still shaking; his knucklebones on the stool between the cots. **Continuity for slot 2:** Darrow's walk down the hall and back was early in the night, before he slept; "nobody passed" covers the hours after. Benedek is not on the page in this Between.

**10/12, ch02:between-4 (*Him Who Can Stand*):** knucklebones for a story told true (the game's second time; Finesse 11 on the nose). Thread 13: Hollis's hands steady while they hold something and shake when they don't (on the page now, twice); he chanted "the bones go to him who can stand" and heard it. His confession: at the window he thought it good, for a heartbeat, that the Captain kneel for the rest (callback **c02.4a**, `later`: fire where Hollis must stand by Darrow at a cost, or the kneeling is put to Darrow in his hearing; it feeds `r.b4.hollis_lives` in spirit, never by number). Darrow's line, "I had three heartbeats in that river. I know what a man can think in one": the Three Heartbeats named by him to Hollis for the first time, as a measure, not a telling; nothing of Aldric's horse (thread 1 untouched). The chair, the Seated Blade and the Measured Hand stay unspoken: the bones were a game, not a lesson. Two Betweens after ch02:s1 are now written; anything more before slot 2 is two lines. **Continuity for slot 2:** both Betweens fall early in the night; Darrow slept after; Benedek is on the page in neither.

**Revised 10/12 (editorial pass on ch02 Betweens 3 and 4; the roll, the ledger deltas and the slots unchanged):** each Between now changes an obligation. *Same Paper*: the three disagree (the oldest: "You. Deciding"; the second would take Marrant's bargain if there were one and says so; the old one's "backs" line stands), Darrow drops the order and asks, and promises **"You'll be asked"** (c02.3a now carries that promise; sister to Wren's c02.1a). *Him Who Can Stand* opens on the first ("They wouldn't let me go down for them." / "Would you?"); the game is compressed; the confession hurts first ("You wanted me to go." "For a moment." "And now?"), Hollis's now is that he would carry Darrow down the Steps himself before Marrant had him, then the heartbeats line, then the full name and Hollis's oath to say the next such thought aloud (**"Out loud. Bells help me"**; c02.4a carries it: fire where he keeps a thought he swore to say, or stands by Darrow at a cost). The Between rules were changed the same day (`/play` §3, `style.md` §3, `design.md` §9): every Between changes an understanding, a relationship or a small obligation.

**10/12 close (ch02:s2, *Feast Bread*, colour mild):** b1.2 slot 2 on the page. `benedek_hollowed` set. Thread 12: Benedek found at the dawn bell of the feast, breathing, eyes open, frost on his lips, no oath; at the word the hall looked to the door, and Darrow kept its eyes on the lad instead. Maelis found the chip of black glass under the tongue, "The far cots never had this" (her only line; the glass is in her coat; it is NOT named Oathstone anywhere: T1 stays). Hollis took the lad's hand in both of his and paid c02.4a: "Out loud, Captain. Since I swore it. I told him to get some sleep." Thread 13: his hands steady while they hold the lad's. Nobody passed (one answer, the row's: the oldest Ninth man by the fire at the gate end, awake: the Captain early and back, the lamp on its round in the small hours, losing its place at Hollis's snoring, which echoes the 10/12 glimpse; slot 3 still owns the far cots, the doors, the keys, the night novice). **World move spent here:** "the kitchen has started counting loaves against the feast's sixty" (the loaves counted aloud and recounted); do not use it again as a missed-day opener. Feast: the bread went down to the gate under the grey cloaks' eyes; whether they took it is on no page (the kitchen's book was never settled). Lore: house.ysolde spoken (a lay brother's "Saint Ysolde's bread"; another's scoff, revised 10/12: "a bone-setter with a bad temper and a bell. Call her saint to her face and you'd have got the bell").

**Revised 10/12, later (ch02:s2):** the word *Hollowed* now gets its common gloss where the page first says it, in Darrow's head (lore `age.hollowing`, the received version only: knights come home breathing, nobody behind the eyes, sent up a mountain with a chit and a lamp; the far cots are where they end). Ch 1 Sc 1's old line ("for the Hollowed or the dying") was cut in the 10/11 pass, so this is the page's first. T4 untouched. The lore-touch cap was lifted the same day (doctrine 1, `style.md` §2): no fixed count, as many as the scene's meaning needs.

**10/12, ch02:between-5 (*Wrong Question*):** Darrow asked Maelis what the glass was; she withheld (question for question, then a flat order) and he said the true thing: under the bell's law a Hollowed man has no will to be taken against, so Marrant could take the lad down without breaking it (his reading of Marrant's far-cots line, thread 12/16, now spoken, to Maelis only; **c02.5a** due at ch02:s3 as his private dread). The glass: "Not the far cots' sickness" and the rest when she knows it, not in the hall (she neither names it nor says she doesn't know: T1 untouched; her pipe out of her teeth is the only tell). Order: the slow way every time, or Wren counts his steps (**c02.5b**, later). Job: make Hollis eat, he won't for her (an opening for a second Between with Hollis that is not his question: slot 5's invitation stays his to bring). Maelis +1 (candour, witnessed).

**10/12, ch02:between-6 (*One Hand*):** the second Between of the feast morning, because of the first (Maelis's job). Thread 13 on the page a third time: Hollis's hands are still only while they hold something; he would not let go of the lad because letting go means the hall sees the shake (never said aloud; the reader infers). Darrow read it (the knucklebones), held the lad's hand for the length of a loaf and filled Hollis's with bread; Hollis ate like a man after a battle. "He's Sixth." / "I know whose he is." Obligation **c02.6a** (later): "Tell her I ate. Don't tell her how" (fire where Maelis asks how, or where the hall sees his hands empty). Hollis +3 (hearth witnessed +2, the kindness +1): chapter Between net +5 of 6; **Hollis is now 43: r.b2.hollis_sober (45) and r.b4.hollis_lives (50) are near, and the next moves should come from choices, not Betweens.** Hearth/Banner −3 (even). Slot 5's invitation (his lie to the lad; witchcraft vs his own eyes) untouched: he asked nothing. The kitchen's book got the half loaf. Both Betweens after ch02:s2 are now written.

**Revised 10/12, later (ch02:between-5):** the argument is pulled out of Darrow in beats ("The lad can't answer now." / the law and Marrant's line / Maelis waits twice / "Marrant can carry that lad down the Steps tomorrow" alone); the reader completes "no will" before he says the consequence. "That isn't an answer" (a verbatim repeat of between-2) is replaced by "How long?", which she leaves unanswered before retreating to the knee. Same events, same ledger (c02.5, c02.5a/b unchanged).

**10/13 close (ch02:s3, *Nobody Passed*, colour mild):** slot 3, challenge **won 2/2, strain 0** (night novice, Warden's Eye: 21 vs 12; the kitchen, Mender's Patience: 21 vs 11; Wren's count unrolled, shown as the confirmation). Result in the ledger: c02.7, due **c02.7a at ch02:climax** (the House has the Captain's account first; Maelis +1). **The Grey Cot** defined on the page: the far cots' grey blanket brought to Benedek because Hollis would not let him be carried to the far cots. Marrant's word on the page as hearsay via the bread-carriers: *ember witchcraft* (thread 16). Fired c02.5a (his private dread, one paragraph) and the callback c02.5b (Wren reads his steps to Maelis at every bell). Kept off the page: the undercroft, "below" (Wren cut off at "So it came from—"), the candle's lean, the east wall, Maelis's thread (the kitchen blames her only for finding the glass). Night novice: unnamed, wick soot on her fingers, watched the door all night from the far lamp; the kitchen: the flour-armed novice who ran the book, the flour skin at the hall door, the old cook who eats the crusts. Keys: "hanging where they hang", nine on the Prior's ring (b1.4's stores key is not said to be on it). Thread 13: Hollis to the hand, "Nobody" (he hears what it means).

**10/13, ch02:between-7 (*The Book*):** the kitchen's book (the flour-armed novice; a ledger, odds in pencil) taking odds on the next Hollowing: Hollis 4, the Captain 5, the kitchen 20, the Grey Cot unpriced. Her reason: a number can be rubbed out; otherwise it is in the dark with the rest of us. Darrow's bet: NOBODY, his chore the ovens if another cot goes grey before the thaw; if none, the kitchen rubs out every price (callback **c02.8a**). **Watch:** q1.farcots (frost on one far-cot mouth) and Hollow Night are not a *new cot going grey*: the bet is lost only by a new Hollowing in the hall. No dice (a wager, not a game). Two Betweens may follow Scene 3; this is the first.

**10/13, ch02:between-8 (*The Far Lamp*):** the second Between after Scene 3, because of the first (the novice had put a wick on nobody). Darrow asked to sit the far lamp (asking, as he promised his men; not c02.3a's fire). Nothing happened on the page: no frost, no heads turning, no flame leaning (q1.farcots and slot 7 keep those). The novice slept; he kept the lamp; soot on his fingers as on hers. Due **c02.9a at ch02:s4**: the next scene opens with him short of sleep and soot in his creases (Rae's scene: she notices hands; one clause). Bearing Hearth/Banner −4: **leans Hearth** now (the site shows it in words). Both Betweens after ch02:s3 are written.

threads.note: the siege's first night; the kitchen's loaves and the feast's bread under his eyes are Ch 2's first world moves. 02:s4: the grey cloak on Rae's box got down for her without a word; the camp has flour to the thaw and past it; the first letter came up with Rae.

note: Rae's interlude (slot 8), the bottom of the Steps that Scene 4 cut past. She does not count; the grey cloak gets off her box for her and she lets him think it was manners; whose boots are dry (his) and whose wet (the winch-brothers'); the House's wood up his chimney; the camp read by its flour (six to the thaw and past it: they mean to stay). The letter from the grey cloak's hand, the rank said twice like a horse already bought: the reader learns why she will not use it. She weighed leaving it on the cage overnight and carried it inside her shirt, wax inward (an echo of Hollis's wax). Darrow's name said first to Hob. Kept off: her father, the rope and the splice, the Market, the tags, the debt, the uncle, the grandmother; the grey thought of only as not thought of (nothing of the mare living, where, or what it costs her). The off ox is named Dun on the page. Revised 10/14: it opens 'That morning, with Wren up on the gate wall counting her down' and ends 'started back up the Steps … a long climb to the dusk bell', so the reader knows it steps back over the day Scene 4 skipped.
next_must_know: Rae is in the House tonight and goes down in the morning. The letter is under Darrow's mattress, wax whole, unread; Hollis knows it came. Darrow does not know a grey cloak handed it to her ('It came up with me'). Slot 5: he reads it by the brazier and burns it; Hollis watches the wax and says nothing, and leaves on the beech leg.

note: Between 9 (Rae, the kitchen, Wed night): the odds moved (c02.8a fired); Rae's stake on NOBODY (c02.10b); she would not name the hand the letter came from, on a carter's principle, and told him to read it and ask again (c02.10a). Nothing of the grey, her father, the rope, the Market or the debt. Her discretion about whose hand a load came out of is in character and plants nothing on its own.
